newsitem.title: EGYPT: Housing, cement, mills shares boost Egypt bourse.
newsitem.headline: Housing, cement, mills shares boost Egypt bourse.

text.p: Cairo's stock exchange rose on Wednesday helped by vigorous demand for housing, cement and mills shares.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index gained 1.32 points to 278.19. The index slipped on Monday for the first time since it broke record highs last week, but it has lost no time reversing the fall since then.
"This is a healthy sign which means the market is stabilising," said broker Neveen el-Tahry of Delta EAB. "Demand is still there and prices are still reasonable. They are not overvalued."

Heliopolis Housing and Development had the highest turnover, accounting for about 9.0 million pounds of the day's 46.48 million pound ($13.67 million) volume. Shares gained 26.75 pounds to close at 245.
The rest of trade concentrated mainly on cement and milling shares, although some of their prices fell.
Broker Elwy Taymour of Hermes-EFG said there was some profit-taking in the mills sector.

Tora Cement slipped 0.50 pounds to 73.00 and privatised Amriyah Cement 0.25 to 65.75. They were second and third-placed shares in terms of turnover with 4.64 million pounds and 3.51 million changing hands respectively.
Central Egypt Flour Mills was the most popular milling share. It shed 2.00 pounds to close at 70.80 pounds.
Of a total 66 stocks traded, 20 rose, 22 fell and the rest closed unchanged.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 433.1 points from Monday's 433.24 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 191.67 from 190.17 points.
